package_info.why_malicious: The package is a typosquatted, homoglyph-impersonating clone of a legitimate UI library, but with .NET DLLs patched via IL weaving to inject a malicious module initializer. This initializer acts as a downloader for second-stage malware (SeroXen RAT), and the package contains no legitimate functionality beyond the attack chain.

malicious_snippets.code_behavior: At module load (import-time), the code downloads a batch script from a hardcoded C2 server, writes it to a temporary file, and executes it, resulting in the retrieval and execution of second-stage malware.

malice_analysis.why_suspicious: The code executes automatically upon module load, downloads and executes remote code from an attacker-controlled server, and is obfuscated to evade detection.
malice_analysis.violated_expectations: Legitimate UI libraries should not contain module initializers that perform network operations or execute arbitrary code. Module initializers are typically used for benign setup, not for launching downloaders.
malice_analysis.similar_legitimate_use: Module initializers may be used for legitimate pre-initialization tasks, such as setting up logging or configuration, but never for downloading and executing remote scripts.
key_indicators: Presence of a module initializer in <Module> pseudo-class
Obfuscated string handling to hide URLs
Network access to hardcoded C2 domain
Writes and executes a batch file at runtime

attack_chain.action: User installs or loads the malicious NuGet package, causing the patched DLL to be loaded.
The module initializer executes automatically, downloading a batch script from the attacker's C2 server.
attack_chain.leads_to: Batch script is written to disk and executed.

attack_chain.action: The batch script (second stage) is executed, which installs the SeroXen RAT or other payloads.
attack_chain.leads_to: System compromise and remote access for the attacker.

behavioral_signatures: Presence of module initializers in <Module> pseudo-class of .NET DLLs
Automatic network requests to hardcoded domains at module load
Obfuscated string handling to hide URLs or commands
DLLs that download and execute batch scripts or other code at load time
file_indicators: Patched .NET DLLs with module initializers not present in upstream/legitimate versions
DLLs containing obfuscated strings or code in <Module> pseudo-class
Temporary batch files written and executed at runtime
network_indicators: Outbound HTTP(S) requests to nazi.igboat.com or similar attacker-controlled domains
Unexpected network activity from UI library DLLs at load time
detection_knowledge.how_to_detect: Scan .NET DLLs in NuGet packages for the presence of module initializers in the <Module> pseudo-class, especially those containing obfuscated strings or network operations. Monitor for unexpected network requests from DLLs at module load, and flag packages that download and execute remote scripts. Compare package contents to legitimate upstream versions to detect IL weaving or binary patching. Watch for homoglyph typosquatting in package names.
